supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39 UTC, ivy.chen ran PowerShell from the interactive Explorer session to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; a file-create event confirms c.zip was created.

At 13:45 UTC, ivy.chen launched Chrome to quickshare-drop.net. The proxy recorded a successful CONNECT with 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes and only 8,800 server-to-client bytes; Zeek independently recorded about 51 MB sent through the proxy connection.

The archive creation was followed within minutes by a large outbound transfer to a file-sharing-style destination that is not among the services listed as approved in the supplied environment context. This combination strongly supports unauthorized data exfiltration.

known_telemetry_limitations: The destination connection is logged as a TLS tunnel; these records do not expose the uploaded request, filename, or content. The proxy records the domain and byte counts, not proof of the payload's identity. (T039-00138, T039-00140)

The evidence confirms c.zip was created and a large transfer followed, but does not directly link that file to the transfer or establish the archive's size and contents. (T039-00104, T039-00106, T039-00138, T039-00140)
claims_not_established: It is not established that c.zip, or any particular client files, were the data sent to quickshare-drop.net. (T039-00104, T039-00106, T039-00138, T039-00140)
The records do not establish Ivy Chen's intent, whether the transfer had an authorized business purpose, or who controlled the destination service. (T039-00133, T039-00138)
The evidence does not establish whether the remote service retained or made the transferred data available to others. (T039-00138, T039-00140)
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine c.zip, including its size, contents, timestamps, and any available file hash; verify whether the source files were accessed and included.
Obtain proxy or TLS inspection records, if available, that identify the upload request, destination account, filename, or payload metadata.
Review endpoint browser history, downloads, and relevant file-access telemetry to corroborate whether c.zip was selected or uploaded.
Confirm with Ivy Chen and the relevant data owner whether the transfer was authorized and had a legitimate business purpose.
Investigate quickshare-drop.net and any associated account or recipient information using available organizational and threat-intelligence sources.
